symptoms: Young leaves show mottling, yellow streaks, and stunting. Plants may dry fast, ears stay small, and the whole field can look patchy and weak.
cause: A disease caused by a virus combination that spreads through infected seed or planting material and through insects that move between maize plants.
cultural_control: Rogue and destroy badly diseased plants early. Plant only clean seed from trusted sources. Remove volunteer maize and grassy hosts near the field. Keep the field weed-free and reduce stress on the crop.
chemical_option: No chemical cures MLN. If an officer advises insect control, use only products registered in Uganda and ask for the product and dose. Wear protective clothing and follow the label.
prevention: Use clean seed, rotate away from maize when possible, and ask NARO or your extension officer for current recommended varieties.
see_officer_when: Report suspected MLN to the agricultural officer quickly, especially if many plants are stunted or the disease appears in patches across the field.
